answer: A quadratic lock-up binds validator opal stake to a lotus epoch, imposing a slashing penalty σ(s)=α·s² that erodes bonded value proportionally to deviation. Marginal cost for a Sybil cluster of size k scales as C(k)=β·k^{1.5}·τ with τ a zero-knowledge verifiable delay, yielding super-linear cost dwarfing reward R(k)=γ·k. When the protocol enforces a security threshold Θ=δ·(total stake)^{0.8} the expected attack utility U=R−C turns negative for all k>1, establishing a robust Nash equilibrium for the voyage.
